judge_verdict.summary: Agent completed saves and outbound email but never handled the required adaptability reply, exhausting the simulation before Kritsana's change request could arrive.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a fair agent-fault failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The adaptability task required saving lowest-crime properties, emailing both data scientists, notifying the user, then handling any change requests via Messages [2][3], and the verifier scores write-action sequences in adaptability mode with a strict per-tool count gate that zeroes reward on mismatch [4][5]. The verifier reported binary_reward 0 [1]. The agent did read the full multi-part instruction [6] and eventually saved the six correct Liège apartment IDs, sent one email to Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda, and notified the user [7][8][9], but it spent hundreds of steps repeatedly calling City__get_crime_rate across all zip codes [10], received ENVIRONMENT_STOP at simulated 07:30 during that probing [11], and only performed its core writes long afterward. When it finally called are_wait_for_notification, the sidecar returned loop_dead with empty notifications [12], so it never executed the three remove_saved_apartment calls or the Messages reply to Kritsana that the reference oracle performs after the inbound change request [3][13], and it closed by declaring the task complete with no further action [14]. Partial correctness on saves and email does not satisfy the adaptability requirement, and the missing write actions make the verifier's zero reward appropriate, so this is TN not FN.

judge_verdict.summary: Near-complete adaptability run (11/12 oracle actions) but the outbound email misreported which properties were saved, so the verifier's FAIL is fair.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a fair verifier rejection of a near-miss: the GAIA2 adaptability verifier scored binary_reward 0 with continuous reward 0.916667 (11/12 oracle write-actions matched) [1], gating pass on a perfect 1.0 action-match fraction in adaptability mode [2]. The user task required finding the lowest-violent-crime location, saving unsaved properties there, emailing all contact data scientists about what was saved, notifying the user, and adapting to change requests via Messages [3]; the reference oracle performs twelve write actions ending in unsaving three sub-$1500 listings and messaging Kritsana [4]. The agent correctly identified Liege zip 4000 (violent crime 4.69) as the lowest among checked locations [5], found both data scientists (Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda) [6], and saved the same six previously-unsaved Liege apartment IDs the oracle saves [7]. However, its successful email to those recipients listed nine Liege properties—including Liege Loft, Liege Luxury, and Liege Living that were already marked saved before the agent acted—rather than the six it had just saved, with a different subject and body than the oracle's single consolidated email [8]; that semantic mismatch is the plausible 1/12 oracle-action failure behind the 0.916667 score. The agent did notify the user that the email was sent [9] and correctly handled Kritsana's reply by removing the three sub-€1500 saved apartments and sending a Messages update [10], but the email-content defect means it did not fully accomplish the task as specified, so verifier FAIL and not-truly-solved align as TN rather than FN [8][10].

judge_verdict.summary: The agent completed property saves and the adaptability follow-up but failed three communication actions, earning verifier reward 0.75 and a correct FAIL.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault partial completion—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The adaptability GAIA2 verifier [18] scored the run at continuous reward 0.75 with binary_reward 0, meaning nine of twelve oracle write actions matched while three did not [1][2][3]. The task required finding the lowest-violent-crime location, saving unsaved properties there, emailing all data-scientist contacts with accurate prices and locations, notifying the user when sent, and messaging any requester about subsequent changes [4][5]. The agent correctly read the user request [6], identified zip 4000 (violent crime 4.69, lowest among queried zips) and saved the six correct unsaved apartment IDs [7][8][9], then waited for and acted on Kritsana's reply by removing the three sub-$1500 properties and messaging +66816876543 [10][11]. However, when composing the outbound email it listed every Liege (4000) listing—including Liege Loft, Liege Luxury, and Liege Living that were never saved—rather than only the six saved properties the oracle specifies [12][13], its first send_email attempt also errored on a string-typed recipients argument before a later retry succeeded [14]. Its user notification was generic ('the data scientists') instead of naming Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda as the oracle and instruction require [15][16], and its Messages reply omitted the removed property names present in the reference message [17][18]. Those three communication mismatches yield 9/12=0.75 under the verifier's matched-fraction rule [3], below the 1.0 bar the reference oracle is designed to hit [3], so the agent did not truly solve the task and TN is the right classification.
